messages:
annah: New contributor hit auth+retry weirdness while porting an example to the Ruby SDK. Token rotating via a small daemon; first call after rotation sometimes 401 then immediate success on retry. Minimal repro attached. Anyone have a concise mitigation?

kevin: Which HTTP client are you using in the example? Behavior differs between net-http, httpx and faraday. Also are you reusing the client instance or creating it per-request?

annah: Using httpx and reusing one client instance to avoid churn. The daemon simply writes the new token to a file.

phil: Sounds like a pooled connection returning a request with stale Authorization metadata. Two pragmatic fixes: 1) read token per-request in the toy example (low effort), or 2) expose a small API on the SDK to invalidate auth cache + reset connection pool for programmatic rotation.

kevin: I like 2) for SDK parity — node/go have hooks for refresh. We could add `client.refresh_token!(new_token)` that clears cached header and resets pools. That keeps perf default but gives an escape hatch.

annah: That would be ideal. For the sample app maybe do per-request reads and note the perf tradeoff in the README so new devs don't hit this. I'll update quickstart.

phil: For tests: add a tiny fork-based integration that simulates daemon writing token after parent forks to reproduce binstub-style races. That CI test can run only in the integration matrix to avoid slowing unit runs.

ci-bot: github/actions - ruby-sampleapp CI queued (integration, unit, lint)

docs-bot: Suggestion: add a short troubleshooting entry to docs "First request 401 after token rotation" with exact env flags to try and recommended file perms (0600).

kevin: I'll open a draft SDK PR that adds `refresh_token!`, an opt-in ENV `RB_TOKEN_REFRESH=per_request` and a unit test that asserts header rebuilt. Will also include a small note in changelog about behavior and migration guidance.

annah: Thanks both. I'll push a readme update for quickstart and link to the PR for people following along. Will report back if the intermittent repro disappears with the SDK change.
